items.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: He turned 90 that day, with Bucky Pizzarelli also, he was playing guitar. It was a wonderful performance.

ctx.x: As I was saying before the cameras were rolling, I’m used to interviewing people that could be my grandfather or grandmother, I’m not so used to interviewing someone who could be my daughter, which says something about my age I guess. But it’s a pleasure to have you here and I know you’ve been getting quite a good deal of press lately. How about just telling me about your most recent meaningful gig for you.

Well the most recent one was at the end of February, at the Academy of Music in Northampton, Massachusetts. And we were playing for Claude Williams’ 90th birthday, Claude “Fiddler” Williams. He turned 90 that day, with Bucky Pizzarelli also, he was playing guitar. It was a wonderful performance. The place was packed, and it was the most recent gig.
So you had what — 75 years age difference, 74, 75, between you and Claude.
